title: Measurement and control of the interaction frequency shift in bosonic optical lattice clocks
authors: J. P. Salvatierra, M. Barbiero, G. Bertaina, D. Calonico, F. Levi, M. G. Tarallo
abstract: We report precise measurements of inter-level interactions in a bosonic optical lattice clock based on $^{88}$Sr atoms. We observe a nonlinear density dependence of the clock shift, even without reaching quantum degeneracy. In a 2D lattice, the Rabi line shape exhibits an interaction sideband consistent with a collective spin model, while in a 1D lattice the shift is modified by density-induced dephasing. These findings, combined with a careful choice of interrogation detuning and atomic density, can enable operation at a net-zero systematic density shift in $^{88}$Sr lattice clocks. We discuss the implications of these findings in many-body physics, quantum simulation, and precision isotope shift measurements, which provide a powerful probe for new physics beyond the Standard Model.
summary: This paper reports on high-precision measurements characterizing interaction frequency shifts in bosonic optical lattice clocks using $^{88}	ext{Sr}$ atoms. By analyzing the nonlinear density dependence of the clock shift in both 1D and 2D lattices, the authors demonstrate a method to actively tune out these systematic collisional shifts at specific operating points. This capability is vital for realizing next-generation quantum sensors with unprecedented stability.
main_problem: The research focuses on precisely measuring and controlling the nonlinear interaction frequency shifts (collisional shifts) experienced by bosonic atoms trapped in optical lattices.
main_result: The study demonstrates that these interactions lead to a density-dependent clock shift, but crucially shows that this shift can be canceled at specific operating points (magic densities/detunings) in both 1D and 2D lattice geometries.
method: The authors combine precise experimental measurements of Rabi line shapes and sideband spectroscopy with theoretical modeling using mean-field approximations derived from full many-body Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system is a bosonic optical lattice clock utilizing $^{88}	ext{Sr}$ atoms, modeled by an effective spin Hamiltonian incorporating linear and nonlinear interaction terms. The dynamics are analyzed via both unitary Schrödinger equations and dissipative optical Bloch equations.
key_observables: Clock shift dependence on atomic density ($N$), Rabi line shapes, and the reconstructed interaction sideband structure.
important_parameters: Interaction energy scales ($U_{ee}, U_{eg}$), lattice dimensionality (1D vs 2D), and specific cancellation detunings ($\delta_{	ext{lock}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations, adiabatic elimination techniques for radial degrees of freedom, and assumptions about the thermal state independence from spin dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Rabi spectroscopy showing asymmetric line shapes in 2D lattices and frequency shift measurements versus total atom number in 1D lattices, confirming interaction effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general Hamiltonian for interacting bosons, deriving effective spin models via adiabatic elimination (theory), and then applying these frameworks to analyze experimental data from 1D and 2D lattice clocks to quantify density shifts and cancellation points (experiment).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of precision measurement in AMO physics by quantifying complex, many-body interactions that must be precisely modeled and controlled for next-generation quantum sensors.
